summary: The reporting implementation correctly uses biological specimens for between-group inference, keeps nuclei nested within specimens, reports specimen counts and metric-specific missingness, provides median differences, Cliff's delta, bootstrap confidence intervals, permutation p-values, and BH-FDR correction, and separates raw count, sampled exposure, and normalized density. Pilot CSV, JSON, spreadsheet, PDF, and track-table values agree within floating-point serialization precision. Acceptance is nevertheless conditional because the declared below-2-um sensitivity population has not been classified or analyzed, and primary body-width outcomes used by study comparisons are omitted from specimen_summary.csv and retained only in specimen_technical_qc.csv.

findings.title: Declared short-track sensitivity analysis remains unresolved
findings.impact: The primary count and morphology summaries include a large, potentially fragment-enriched below-2-um stratum. Without blinded classification and a specimen-level sensitivity summary, the robustness of count, density, and morphology outcomes to this population is unknown. This prevents an unconditional statistics/reporting pass for a production candidate.
evidence: V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:53-58 identifies 831 KJ-01 and 560 WT-01 below-2-um tracks and defers their review.
audits/claims_registry.json claim PIPELINE-V571-PRODUCTION-001 lists classified sensitivity review as a known limitation.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:7211-7259 includes all technical-valid tracks in the primary summaries without a reported short-track sensitivity counterpart.
findings.recommendation: Complete blinded technical classification of the below-2-um stratum across specimens, preserve the technical-valid primary population, and report specimen-level primary-versus-classified-sensitivity effects for count, both densities, and morphology metrics.

findings.title: Primary study specimen table omits body-width outcomes used in comparisons
findings.impact: The study comparison CSV/PDF can report body-width outcomes that are absent from specimen_summary.csv. The underlying values remain available in specimen_technical_qc.csv, but placing primary biological morphology outcomes only in a technical-QC table weakens report-to-source traceability and misclassifies their role.
evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12271-12295 computes specimen-level body width, P90 width, area-length width, length/body-width ratio, and width availability.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12351-12357 includes body-width metrics in between-specimen comparisons.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12980-13008 omits those body-width fields from biological_columns written to specimen_summary.csv while writing the full frame to specimen_technical_qc.csv.
findings.recommendation: Add the primary body-width fields used by group comparisons to specimen_summary.csv, retaining only genuinely technical diagnostics in specimen_technical_qc.csv, and add a test asserting every comparison metric is present in the primary specimen source table.

findings.title: Group-level descriptive summary does not expose metric-specific non-missing specimen counts
findings.impact: Comparison tables report reference_n and comparison_n correctly, but group_summary.csv reports only total specimen_count. Readers using the group summary alone cannot distinguish total specimens from the available denominator for each metric.
evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12338-12347 reports one specimen_count per group while dropping missing values separately for each metric.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12501-12502 correctly reports metric-specific sample sizes in the comparison table.
findings.recommendation: Add <metric>_n columns to group_summary.csv or clearly direct users to specimen_group_comparisons.csv for metric-specific denominators.
